short: The first British Asian prime minister, installed to steady the markets.
full:
Rishi Sunak became prime minister on 25 October 2022, unopposed, after Boris Johnson withdrew from the contest to replace Liz Truss. A former analyst and hedge fund partner, he had been chancellor through the pandemic and devised the furlough scheme that paid the wages of nearly twelve million workers. He was the first British Asian and the first Hindu to hold the office, and at forty-two the youngest since Lord Liverpool in 1812.

His stated priorities were halving inflation, growing the economy and stopping small boats crossing the Channel. Inflation fell from over eleven per cent to under three, but the plan to deport asylum seekers to Rwanda was struck down by the Supreme Court and never carried out. He agreed the Windsor Framework with the European Union in 2023, easing the Northern Ireland protocol, and cancelled the northern leg of HS2. He called an election for July 2024 and lost 251 seats.
